newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Espirito Santo state lowers coffee estimate.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Espirito Santo state lowers coffee estimate.

text.p: Brazil's Espirito Santo state should produce 3.38 million 60-kg bags coffee in 1997/98, down from a previous estimate of 3.59 million bags published in December, according to the state agricultural secretariat.
The forecast is also 31.97 percent lower than the 4.97 million bags produced in 1996/97, the secretariat said.
Output of arabica coffee is now expected to reach 900,000 bags against a previous forecast of 1.06 million bags.
Conillon coffee production is estimated at 2.48 million bags, also down from a previous figure of 2.53 million.
Production of arabica and robusta coffee in 1996/97 was 1.69 million and 3.28 million bags, respectively.
Other recent trade estimates for the state have been between 3.4 million and 4.15 million bags.

The fall in output is due to the on-off cycle particularly in arabica coffee which sees a smaller crop every other year, said Marcos Moulin, agronomist at the department responsible for the state's crop estimates.
In addition the late arrival of rains hit bean-setting this year which has only become apparent in the last few months.
"The setting has turned out to be not so good as we originally thought," Moulin said.
The preliminary outlook for the 1998/99 crop looks very good, however, Moulin said.

"If we have the right conditions we could have a supercrop in 1998...It is just speculation at this stage but we think Espirito Santo could produce a crop of six million bags, 4.2 million conillon and 1.8 million arabica," he added.
The secretariat's next estimate for 1997/98 harvest is due in September, he said. ((-Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151))
